RoomType.rationale: KnightsElite.cs:12 `RoomType => RoomType.Elite`. Modeled structurally by pool membership. One shared mechanism across this batch; see `encounter/_room_type_and_weak` in the report.

Tags.rationale: KnightsElite.cs:14 `Tags => [EncounterTag.Knights]`. The sim's `Encounter` dataclass has no `Tags` field; the game's tag-avoidance mechanic (`EncounterModel.SharesTagsWith`, EncounterModel.cs:279-286, consumed by `ActModel.AddWithoutRepeatingTags`'s `GrabBag`) is instead modeled at the ROOM-POOL level: `ActRooms.tags` (rooms.py:51-65) maps an encounter id to its tag tuple, transcribed from the C# `EncounterTag` declarations (rooms.py:197-199's own comment names the source: "the two Scrolls of Biting variants share EncounterTag.Scrolls, Knights carries EncounterTag.Knights"), and `_shares_tags`/`_grab_without_repeating_tags`/`_add_without_repeating_tags` (rooms.py:243-256, :357-373) consult it when picking the next elite room, refusing a same-tag repeat exactly like the game's GrabBag predicate. EXECUTED (read, not merely declared): `_grab_without_repeating_tags` (rooms.py:357-373) builds its exclusion predicate as `k != last and not _shares_tags(self.rooms, k, last)` and passes it to `grab_and_remove` (sts2_rl/rng.py:333-349), the parity port of `GrabBag.GrabAndRemove` -- so the tag check is load-bearing in the actual draw, not decorative. Cross-referenced to `seam/rooms_and_map`, which owns the encounter-SELECTION mechanism itself; this record verdicts only whether `knights`' own tag membership is faithfully carried into that mechanism, and it is. Same observable, different architecture -- filed under `encounter/_room_type_and_weak`'s sibling shared id is not needed since Knights is the ONLY unit in this batch with a real tag; recorded here directly.

guards.what: Slot-name assignment on the initial roster: KnightsElite hard-codes "first"/"second"/"third" per creature; the sim's KNIGHTS_ELITE has no `monster_slots`, so all three land at `slot_name=None`
guards.rationale:
CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). The `Encounter` dataclass already had `slots`/`monster_slots` and `CreatureCmd.add(slot_name=)` re-sorts on them (shipped round 7 for Fabricator/Ovicopter); this unit simply never declared its row. It does now, transcribed from the C# `Slots` override and `GenerateMonsters`' `(model, slot)` pairs, and `CombatState.__init__` routes every roster through `Encounter.seat_in_slots` so the seventeen `create_monsters` overrides are seated too. Regression tests: test/test_encounter_slots.py. KnightsElite declares no `Slots` override, so the three names are carried on `monster_slots` alone and the sort stays the no-op the game also runs.

WHAT THE GAP SAID: Filed under shared mechanism `encounter/_slot_order` alongside `encounter/axebots`' dormant slot gap. NOTE: KnightsElite is unusual among slot-naming encounters in that it does NOT override `Slots` at all (base default `Array.Empty<string>()`, EncounterModel.cs:176) -- the three literal slot names in `GenerateMonsters` are never validated against a declared row. Traced both potential readers of `Creature.SlotName` for this content and found neither reachable: (1) `EncounterModel.GetNextSlot` / `Encounter.Slots`-driven resorting never fires for the INITIAL roster at all -- `CombatRoom.StartCombat` (CombatRoom.cs:207-213) calls `CombatState.CreateCreature(monsterModel, CombatSide.Enemy, slot)`, which sets `Creature.SlotName` directly in its constructor (Creature.cs:346-361) and never calls `SortEnemiesBySlotName`; that sort only runs from `CombatManager.AddCreature`, the MID-COMBAT spawn path (`CreatureCmd.Add`), gated on `creature.SlotName != null` (per `monster/fabricator.json`'s already-closed guard on the identical sort). So the initial three knights' list ORDER is exactly `GenerateMonsters`'s return order regardless of their slot names -- confirmed matching above. (2) No content reader: `grep -n SlotName src/Core/Models/Monsters/FlailKnight.cs SpectralKnight.cs MagiKnight.cs` finds nothing, and none of the three knights summons a creature mid-combat (read all three move sets; no `CreatureCmd.Add`/`SummonIntent`-backed spawn exists for any of them) -- so no LATER creature-add could ever trigger a slot-keyed resort in this encounter either. The slot names are therefore pure room-layout metadata (almost certainly a visual left-to-right seating cue for the elite's three-model tableau) with zero mechanical reader on the game side, and the sim's `Encounter`/`Monster` have no visual layer to seat regardless. DORMANT: a genuinely un-ported declarative fact (`monster_slots` should be `("first","second","third")` to be complete), with zero observable consequence found by executing both of the game's own SlotName-reading code paths against this specific content.

guards.what: Draw count / stream independence of the per-encounter Rng

The Niche HP-roll for THREE distinct degenerate ranges in one roster (FlailKnight 101/101, SpectralKnight 93/93, MagiKnight 82/82 -- no duplicated species, so the exclusion-set logic never empties, unlike `encounter/construct_menagerie`)
guards.rationale: Each of the three creatures draws exactly one Niche value over its own single-element candidate set (`hashSet={101}`/`{93}`/`{82}` respectively, none excluded by a sibling since no two knights share an HP value): one `NextItem`/`next_int_range(0,1)` draw each, three total, matching in count and per-creature assignment (combat.py:402-431).

rooms.py:195 lists `knights` in Glory's `elite_keys`, and `KNIGHTS_ELITE` is registered in `sts2_rl/monsters/glory/__init__.py`'s `ENCOUNTERS` dict (line 72).
